title: Ray Charles the jazz artist; a flop Philadelphia date
summary: Thomas learns Ray Charles had played with Lowell Fulsom and was really a jazz artist, and misbooks New York musicians for his first Philadelphia date.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Because I didn't know when I first got involved with Ray Charles that he was a Jazz artist. I just didn't know that. He was singing Rock-and-Roll! And I talked to him one day, and he said, "Well, you know, Walter, I started recording Rock-and-Roll to make money." He knew he was a Jazz artist, but he knew... He had played with Lowell Fulsom, he saw what those R&B...
Lowell Fulsom. He used to be the piano player with Lowell Fulsom.

So we got him a recording date with Atlantic as a single, and he took some off his men out of there, I guess; he got his own men and recorded. And I had the first date to book for him down in Philadelphia, at a club. And I had to get the musicians to play with him. And I made one mistake. I got the musicians from New York. I didn't know Ray Charles was a Jazz artist. Because I'd just heard the songs he was doing, but it wasn't Jazz, and I could have got the Jazz musicians in Philadelphia. Because Philadelphia had more Jazz musicians than New York ever had. All the best Jazz musicians in New York came from somewhere else.
So I booked this date, and it was a flop. Because Ray Charles rehearsed, and the guys wasn't up to par, what he wanted. So he just canceled the date. And it made me put

all of my effort I could on him, to make him as big as I could. Because I had made the mistake by not checking him out to know what he was playing. I found out later on. Because we had to get him to...
